Why is my ios/watchos build on physical device stalled?

~/Developer/luke-device.sh
building main at ddd91a37 refactor(brain): USER.md is the facts store, and the standing context carries the roster and projects alone (#1478)
iphone C44AA64B-A664-5C97-9C2F-FF131A0DBC81
watch  1E423FDD-C802-5360-BF3A-E26B98655C5B
push entitlement: dropped (set LUKE_PUSH=1 to keep it)
xcodebuild… (log: /tmp/luke-device-build.log)
I'll look at the build script and the xcodebuild log to see where it's stuck.

input.description: Show the device build script and the tail of its log

result.output:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build Luke for the connected iPhone (watch app embedded), install and launch on both.
#
#   ~/Developer/luke-device.sh            build the checked-out commit, install, launch
#   ~/Developer/luke-device.sh --pull     fast-forward main first
#   LUKE_PUSH=1 ~/Developer/luke-device.sh   keep the push entitlement (needs a team that can hold it)
#
# Builds the luke checkout you run it from (falls back to ~/Developer/luke). Env: LUKE_REPO, LUKE_TEAM (default 7UHHCDBUK2).
set -euo pipefail

# The repo is the checkout you run this from; ~/Developer/luke only when you are not inside one.
if [ -n "${LUKE_REPO:-}" ]; then
  REPO="$LUKE_REPO"
elif top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) && [ -f "$top/apps/ios/Luke.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj" ]; then
  REPO="$top"
else
  REPO="$HOME/Developer/luke"
fi
TEAM="${LUKE_TEAM:-7UHHCDBUK2}"
OUT=/tmp/luke-device-build
LOG=/tmp/luke-device-build.log
APP="$OUT/Build/Products/Debug-iphoneos/Luke.app"
WATCH_APP="$APP/Watch/LukeWatch.app"
PHONE_BUNDLE=dev.tryluke.ios
WATCH_BUNDLE=dev.tryluke.ios.watchkitapp

cd "$REPO"
if [ "${1:-}" = "--pull" ]; then
  git pull -q --ff-only origin main
fi
echo "building $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD) at $(git log -1 --format='%h %s')"

devices=$(xcrun devicectl list devices 2>/dev/null)
PHONE=$(printf '%s\n' "$devices" | grep -i "iphone" | grep -i "connected" | grep -oE '[0-9A-F]{8}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{12}' | head -1 || true)
WATCH=$(printf '%s\n' "$devices" | grep -i "watch" | grep -i "connected" | grep -oE '[0-9A-F]{8}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{4}-[0-9A-F]{12}' | head -1 || true)
if [ -z "$PHONE" ]; then
  echo "no connected iPhone found; plug it in or unlock it" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "iphone $PHONE"; echo "watch  ${WATCH:-none connected}"

signing=(DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$TEAM")
if [ "${LUKE_PUSH:-0}" != "1" ]; then
  cat > /tmp/luke-no-push.entitlements <<'PLIST'
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict/>
</plist>
PLIST
  signing+=(CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS=/tmp/luke-no-push.entitlements)
  echo "push entitlement: dropped (set LUKE_PUSH=1 to keep it)"
fi

echo "xcodebuild… (log: $LOG)"
if ! xcodebuild -project apps/ios/Luke.xcodeproj -scheme Luke -configuration Debug \
    -destination "platform=iOS,id=$PHONE" -derivedDataPath "$OUT" -allowProvisioningUpdates \
    "${signing[@]}" build > "$LOG" 2>&1; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED" >&2
  grep -E "error:" "$LOG" | sort -u | head -20 >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "build ok"

xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$PHONE" "$APP" > /dev/null
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$PHONE" "$PHONE_BUNDLE" > /dev/null
echo "iphone: installed and launched"

if [ -n "$WATCH" ]; then
  xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$WATCH" "$WATCH_APP" > /dev/null
  xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$WATCH" "$WATCH_BUNDLE" > /dev/null
  echo "watch: installed and launched"
fi

content.text:
The build was never hung. It was sitting in the silent "Resolve Package Graph" phase while it downloaded and unzipped Sentry's binary frameworks, and it has since moved on to compiling.

**What was happening.** Commit `6e8b76a8` (Port iOS and watch telemetry crash reporting to Sentry, #1463, merged today) added `sentry-cocoa` 9.28.0 to `apps/ios/LukeKit/Package.swift`. That package declares seven binary xcframework targets. Xcode's package resolution downloads and extracts every binary target a manifest declares, not only the one product you link, so a first build after that commit pulls roughly 2.2 GB of zips and extracts them. During that phase xcodebuild prints only the "Resolve Package Graph" line, so the log looks frozen. The WebRTC binary was already cached from an earlier build at 15:50, which is why previous runs didn't show this.

**Current state.** While I was watching, the child process was an `unzip` of `Sentry-Dynamic.xcframework.zip`, then the log jumped to `SwiftCompile` steps for PostHog. It has now logged about 2,000 compile and link steps and no errors, so it's a normal build in progress. Your script will print `build ok` and install to the phone and watch when it finishes.

**Going forward.** The Sentry zips are now in `~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm/artifacts`, so subsequent builds skip the download, though the derived-data extraction under `/tmp/luke-device-build` still has to happen once per fresh derived-data path. If you want the script to show progress during resolution in future, drop the redirect to the log or `tail -f /tmp/luke-device-build.log` in another pane while it runs.

fix(watch): explicit self in the voice socket's ready-state lock closure

Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.3.3) refuses the implicit `self` inside the nested
`withLock` closure of the connection's weak-self state handler, so the
LukeWatch target no longer compiled for a device:

  WatchWebSocketChannel.swift:52:33: error: reference to property 'isReady'
  in closure requires explicit use of 'self' to make capture semantics explicit

Verified with a generic watchOS build of the LukeWatch scheme and the full
Debug device build of the Luke scheme on a Mac. CI builds nothing for the
Mac and cannot verify this.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push -q -u origin fix/watch-socket-explicit-self && gh pr create --title "fix(watch): explicit self in the voice socket's ready-state lock closure" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- `WatchWebSocketChannel`'s `.ready` case writes `isReady` inside a nested `withLock` closure of a `[weak self]` handler. Xcode 26.6 (Swift 6.3.3) rejects the implicit `self` there, so the LukeWatch target failed to compile for a device. This names `self` explicitly.

## Verification
- `xcodebuild -scheme LukeWatch -destination 'generic/platform=watchOS'` builds.
- The full Debug device build of the `Luke` scheme (watch app embedded) builds on a Mac.
- CI runs the portable Linux check only and could not verify this; a Mac break is caught at the release rehearsal on a tag. Dean is testing on the physical iPhone and watch before merge.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"
